tagline: The gateway to the south, with long Sai Ri Beach, the Prince of Chumphon's warship, dive islands, and robusta coffee
introHtml:
Chumphon is the first province of the south as you drive down from Prachuap Khiri Khan. Most people treat it as a stopover on the way to Koh Tao and Samui, but the province itself has long beaches, islands to dive around, and fresh seafood. Locals are proud of Prince Abhakara of Chumphon (affectionately called Sadet Tia), and shrines and memorials to him are scattered across several spots.

Beyond the sea, Chumphon grows robusta coffee and fruit like durian and mangosteen. People come here to sleep on quiet beaches, take a boat out to dive the islands, drive along the coast, and stop for roadside seafood. It is a province that is still less crowded than the Andaman side.
bestTime: January–April, when skies are clear and the sea is calm — good for boat dives around the islands and beach days. The rainy season peaks in October–November.

highlights.name: Sai Ri Beach
highlights.blurb: The long beach that is the face of Chumphon. At its far end sit the Prince of Chumphon's shrine and a replica of the warship HTMS Chumphon by the sea — the spot where people come to pay respects to Sadet Tia and take photos.

highlights.name: Sadet Tia, the Prince of Chumphon
highlights.blurb: Admiral Prince Abhakara of Chumphon, revered by locals as the guardian spirit of the city. He has several shrines and memorials around the province, and people commonly come to make vows about work and health.

highlights.name: The Chumphon Islands
highlights.blurb: A cluster of islands off the coast — such as Koh Ngam, Koh Lang Ka Jiew, and Koh Mattra — where you can take a boat out to dive coral reefs and fish. The water is clear and there are still fewer people than on other coasts.

highlights.name: Pak Nam Chumphon and the pier to Koh Tao
highlights.blurb: The Pak Nam area is the main pier where people catch the speedboat onward to Koh Tao, Koh Phangan, and Samui. There are markets and waterfront seafood restaurants to stop at before boarding.

highlights.name: Chumphon robusta coffee
highlights.blurb: Chumphon is one of Thailand's big robusta-growing areas, with coffee farms and cafes that roast their beans locally. Coffee lovers can stop to taste the local robusta at plenty of spots.

highlights.name: Khao Din So and the coastal viewpoints
highlights.blurb: Low hills against the sea around Pathio that look down over the bay and the long beach — a photo stop while driving the coast road in the northern part of the province.

foodScene.name: Fresh seafood
foodScene.note: The whole province sits on the Gulf of Thailand, so fish, squid, prawns, shellfish, and blue swimmer crab come straight off the boats. Restaurants by the sea around Sai Ri Beach and Pak Nam cook it every which way.

foodScene.name: Chumphon mackerel (pla tu)
foodScene.note: These waters are a source of short mackerel — plump and rich. Eat it fried, steamed, or in a sour soup. The fresh markets sell both fresh and sun-dried pla tu to take home.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ya pak tai
foodScene.note: A southern dish easy to find all over town — rice noodles with a punchy southern curry sauce, eaten with fresh raw vegetables. Locals have it for breakfast and lunch all the time.

foodScene.name: Gaeng tai pla and gaeng leuang
foodScene.note: Bold local southern curries — the intense fish-innards curry (gaeng tai pla) and the sour-spicy yellow curry (gaeng leuang) with fish and vegetables, eaten with hot steamed rice.

foodScene.name: Robusta coffee
foodScene.note: This is robusta country — cafes in town and coffee farms brew up local beans with the strong southern roast, served hot or iced, with roasted beans to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Durian and mangosteen
foodScene.note: Chumphon is a major fruit-growing area. In the rainy season there's plenty of Monthong durian and mangosteen, with roadside fruit stalls selling them fresh in season.

foodScene.name: Souvenirs from Pak Nam and the town
foodScene.note: Dried squid, shrimp paste, chili dips, and processed seafood from the Pak Nam Chumphon area are all there to take home — along with the famous dried lady finger bananas.

foodScene.name: Lady finger bananas (kluai lep mu nang)
foodScene.note: A small, slender banana specific to Chumphon — sweet and fragrant, good fresh, but best known dried as the province's signature take-home gift.

attractions.name: Sai Ri Beach
attractions.blurb: The long beach that is Chumphon's main beach — walk along the shore, with beachside restaurants and the Prince of Chumphon's shrine at the far end.

attractions.name: The Prince of Chumphon's shrine and HTMS Chumphon
attractions.blurb: The Sadet Tia shrine beside Sai Ri Beach sits next to a replica of the warship HTMS Chumphon — the city's key spot for paying respects, making wishes, and taking photos.

attractions.name: The Chumphon Islands
attractions.blurb: A cluster of islands off the coast, such as Koh Ngam and Koh Lang Ka Jiew — take a boat out to dive coral reefs, fish, and do the islands as a day trip.

attractions.name: Pak Nam Chumphon
attractions.blurb: The pier and waterfront market area where people connect onward by boat to Koh Tao, with seafood restaurants and a fishing-community feel.

attractions.name: Mu Ko Chumphon National Park
attractions.blurb: A stretch of sea and islands with coral, clear water, and both snorkeling and dive spots — a diving area that is still uncrowded.

attractions.name: Wat Khao Chedi and the city viewpoint
attractions.blurb: A temple on a hill that you climb to make merit and take in a wide view of the town and the sea — a popular viewpoint near the town center.

attractions.name: Pathio tree tunnel
attractions.blurb: A coastal road around Pathio where the trees on both sides curve toward each other into a tunnel — an easy photo stop and a pleasant drive in the north of the province.

attractions.name: Arunothai Beach and Thung Wua Laen Beach
attractions.blurb: Quiet white-sand beaches in the north of the province with clear water and few people — good for lounging on the sand and an easy swim.

itineraryIdeas: Chumphon 2D1N — Sai Ri Beach, the Sadet Tia shrine, and seafood
Chumphon for nature — diving the Chumphon Islands and Thung Wua Laen Beach
Chumphon for cafes — robusta coffee farms and cafes in town
Chumphon as a stopover to Koh Tao and Koh Phangan — one night before the boat
Chumphon to Ranong — cross over for hot springs and the Andaman coast
Chumphon to Prachuap Khiri Khan — drive the coast from Pathio to Bang Saphan
